explanation: Tipping is not obligatory in Indonesia, and many restaurants already add a 5-10% service charge to the bill. Leaving small change or rounding up is a welcomed, polite gesture for good service, especially in tourist-oriented restaurants in places like Jakarta or Bali. Small local warungs (eateries) generally neither expect nor require a tip.
local_tip: Check the bill for an already-included service charge; if there isn't one, rounding up or leaving a modest amount in cash for good service is a nice, optional gesture.
regional_note: Tipping is more common and expected in tourist hubs like Bali and Jakarta than at small local warungs or in rural areas.

also_check.note: Tipping can be seen as insulting; excellent service is the baseline, not something extra to pay for.
15-20% is the standard expected tip for sit-down restaurant service.
Service is included by law, but leaving small extra change for good service is a nice touch.

sources.title: Tipping in Bali: When and How Much to Tip
